```{r cars}
## 1. Get Normalized Counts from DESeq2 object
library(tidyverse)
dds <- readRDS("dds.rds")
counts_norm <- counts(dds, normalized=TRUE)
```

```{r}
## 2. Add Gene Symbols
expr_df <- data.frame(Symbol = rowData(dds)$gene_name, counts_norm)%>%
  filter(!is.na(Symbol) & Symbol != "") %>%
  group_by(Symbol) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean))%>%
  column_to_rownames("Symbol")

expr_df <- readRDS("expr_df.rds")
expr_df
```
```{r}

## 3. Run Deconvolution (using 'epic'). EPIC is excellent for identifying B cells, CD4 T cells, CD8 T cells, Endothelial cells, Macrophages, and NK cells.
# if (!require("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")
# library(remotes)
# remotes::install_github("dviraran/xCell")
# remotes::install_github("cansysbio/ConsensusTME") 
# remotes::install_github("omnideconv/immunedeconv")

library(immunedeconv)
res <- deconvolute(as.matrix(expr_df), "epic")
head(res)
```
```{r}
# 4. Add 'condition' metadata for the plot
library(tidyverse)
meta <- as.data.frame(colData(dds))

if(!"sample" %in% colnames(meta)){
  meta <- meta %>% rownames_to_column("sample")
}
head(meta)
```
```{r}
plot_data <- res %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -cell_type, names_to = "sample", values_to = "score") %>%
  left_join(meta, by = "sample")
plot_data
```
```{r}
# 5. Plot the Immune Landscape
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = condition, y = score, fill = condition)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~cell_type, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Immune Landscape (EPIC Method)", y = "Estimated Fraction")
```
```{r}
head(unique(plot_data$sample))
```
```{r}
head(unique(meta$sample))
```
```{r}
plot_data$sample_clean <- gsub("-", ".", plot_data$sample)
meta$sample_clean <- gsub("-", ".", meta$sample)
```

```{r}
plot_data_final <- plot_data %>%
  select(sample_clean, cell_type, score) %>%  # Keep only the essentials
  left_join(meta %>% select(sample_clean, condition), by = "sample_clean")

# 3. Check if NA is gone
summary(as.factor(plot_data_final$condition))
```
```{r}
clean_tcga <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("-", ".", x)        # Convert dashes to dots
  x <- gsub("^X", "", x)        # Remove leading 'X' if it exists
  x <- substr(x, 1, 12)         # Keep only the first 12 characters (Patient ID)
  return(x)
}

# Apply to EPIC results
plot_data$sample_clean <- clean_tcga(plot_data$sample)

# Apply to Metadata
meta$sample_clean <- clean_tcga(meta$sample)

# Re-run the join
plot_data_final <- plot_data %>%
  select(sample_clean, cell_type, score) %>% 
  left_join(meta %>% select(sample_clean, condition) %>% distinct(), by = "sample_clean")
```
```{r}
print(table(plot_data_final$condition, useNA = "always"))
```
```{r}
ggplot(plot_data_final, aes(x = condition, y = score, fill = condition)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~cell_type, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Normal" = "#999999", "Basal" = "#E41A1C", "HER2" = "#377EB8")) +
  labs(title = "Immune Landscape: HER2 vs Basal vs Normal",
       subtitle = "Method: EPIC Deconvolution",
       y = "Estimated Cell Fraction",
       x = "Group")
```
# IMMUNE CHECKPOINT ANALYSIS

```{r}
library(pheatmap)
library(tidyverse)
library(DESeq2)

# 1. Transform the data for visualization (VST is faster and robust)
vsd <- read_rds("vst.rds")
vst_mat <- assay(vsd)

# 2. Define your "Exhaustion & Activation" gene list
# I've added a few more classic ones (IDO1, HAVCR2) to give a fuller picture
exhaustion_genes <- c("CD274", "PDCD1", "LAG3", "TIGIT", "CTLA4", "HAVCR2", "IDO1", "CD270")

# 3. Filter the matrix for these genes
# We use 'gene_name' from rowData to match your earlier steps
genes_in_data <- rowData(dds)$gene_name # Use the exact column name you used before
target_rows <- which(genes_in_data %in% exhaustion_genes)

# Subset and set symbols as rownames
plot_mat <- vst_mat[target_rows, ]
rownames(plot_mat) <- genes_in_data[target_rows]

anno_col <- as.data.frame(colData(dds)[, c("condition"), drop = FALSE])

# 5. Plot the heatmap
pheatmap(plot_mat, 
         annotation_col = anno_col, 
         main = "T-cell Exhaustion & Checkpoint Landscape",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(100),
         scale = "row",           # Crucial: Shows relative high/low across samples
         show_colnames = FALSE,   # Hides messy sample IDs
         cluster_cols = TRUE,     # Groups samples with similar immune profiles
         cluster_rows = TRUE,     # Groups similar checkpoint genes
         border_color = NA)
```
IMMUNE DECONVOLUTION OF HER2 AND BASAL
```{r}
# 1. Filter dds to keep only Basal and HER2
# (Make sure 'basal' and 'her2' match the exact spelling in your colData)
dds_cancer <- dds[, dds$condition %in% c("Basal", "HER2")]

# 2. Drop the 'normal' level so it doesn't show up as an empty spot in plots
dds_cancer$condition <- droplevels(dds_cancer$condition)

# 3. Extract Normalized Counts for these samples
counts_subset <- counts(dds_cancer, normalized = TRUE)

# 4. Create the expression matrix (using gene_name from rowData)
expr_df <- data.frame(Symbol = rowData(dds_cancer)$gene_name, counts_subset) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Symbol) & Symbol != "") %>%
  group_by(Symbol) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Symbol")
head(expr_df)
```
```{r}
res_cancer <- deconvolute(as.matrix(expr_df), "epic")
```
```{r}
# Preparation of metadata
meta_cancer <- as.data.frame(colData(dds_cancer))
meta_cancer

```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Take your results and pivot them
plot_data <- res_cancer %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -cell_type, names_to = "raw_id", values_to = "score")

# 2. Create a 'clean_id' in the results
plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(clean_id = gsub("-", ".", raw_id)) %>%       # Convert dashes to dots
  mutate(clean_id = gsub("^X", "", clean_id)) %>%    # Remove leading X
  mutate(clean_id = substr(clean_id, 1, 12))         # Keep first 12 characters

# 3. Create a 'clean_id' in your metadata
meta_cancer_clean <- meta_cancer %>%
  mutate(clean_id = gsub("-", ".", sample)) %>%      # Convert dashes to dots
  mutate(clean_id = gsub("^X", "", clean_id)) %>%    # Remove leading X
  mutate(clean_id = substr(clean_id, 1, 12)) %>%     # Keep first 12 characters
  distinct(clean_id, .keep_all = TRUE)               # Remove any duplicates

# 4. Join them
plot_data_final <- left_join(plot_data, meta_cancer_clean, by = "clean_id")

# 5. VERIFY: This should no longer show all NA
print(table(plot_data_final$condition, useNA = "always"))
```
```{r}
# Filter out any lingering NAs just in case
plot_data_final <- plot_data_final %>% filter(!is.na(condition))

#install.packages("ggpubr")
library(ggpubr)

# Ensure condition is treated as a factor for clean plotting
plot_data_final$condition <- as.factor(plot_data_final$condition)

ggplot(plot_data_final, aes(x = condition, y = score, fill = condition)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~cell_type, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_bw() +
  # Use lowercase here if your metadata is lowercase!
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Basal" = "#E41A1C", "HER2" = "#377EB8")) + 
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", label = "p.signif") +
  labs(title = "Immune Landscape: HER2 vs BLBC",
       subtitle = "Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test",
       y = "Estimated Cell Fraction (EPIC)")
```
